messages.author: dc83f318e1e834c9
messages.subject: Covariance >1 in Multigroup model
parts:
Hi Folks,
I specified a SEM in lavaan with 3 latent "outcome" variables (three indicators), one manifest predictor (modeled as pseudo-latent var) as well as gender and age (likewise modeled as pseudo-latent var). Besides the autorcorrelative error specification, I also specified a correlation between the three "outcomes", as they are highly correlated. In the non-multigroup model, everything runs smoothly, fit is fine and correlations between outcomes are within reasonable bounds. However, when I introduce a multigroup factor dividing the sample into uneven groups (108 vs. 49), the fit stays fine but the correlation between the outcomes in one group exceeds 1 (i.e., 1.184, 1.031 and 1.415). Now I am largely worried, that this may indicate a missspecification or just be too complex fo the unbalanced subsamples. So I first fixed the covariances to .99 which made the model fit drop substantially. Interestingly, when I fix variances via std.lv = TRUE, the correlations are within reason and model fit is fine, but I read that using the command means trouble outside of the solely cfa-context (i.e., within a structural model).

Any ideas on how to further investigate? The only idea I can come up with is specifying a latent moderation using the indprod-function, which may reduce the potential problem of the very small subsample (n=49).
